heading: Grokking-like delayed generalization occurs during language-model pretraining and fine-tuning
definition: grokking-like delayed generalization occurs during LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.
summary: Several independent groups report grokking-like delayed generalization during language-model pretraining and fine-tuning, using different measures. Evidence is task-dependent, and scales above 10B parameters remain unresolved.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 below 1B for restricted delayed-generalization measures. R2 at 1–10B across different pretraining and fine-tuning settings; R0 for the specific OLMoE 7B pretraining protocol, with a local C result for multi-fact chaining. ? at 10–100B and >100B. Toy settings are not separately identified in V4 counts.
suggested_status.reason: Independent support comes from BERT OOD fine-tuning (arXiv:2403.03942#R1), Llama copying during pretraining (arXiv:2409.09281#r1), OLMoE domain-level delayed generalization and paired math trajectories (arXiv:2506.21551#r1, arXiv:2506.21551#r2, arXiv:2506.21551#r3, arXiv:2506.21551#r4, arXiv:2506.21551#r5), and knowledge-graph intersection fine-tuning (arXiv:2607.08393#T25, arXiv:2607.08393#T27, arXiv:2607.08393#T29, arXiv:2607.08393#T31). OLMoE's local, asynchronous domain gains support V4; the claim requires neither a sharp global jump nor synchrony. Its paired-group result remains conditional on retrospective grouping and LoRA instruction-tuned evaluation. BERT support includes additional HANS subcases shown in Appendix C Figure 10; the HANS failure condition is restricted to subcases not shown there (arXiv:2403.03942#R1). QQP/PAWS-QQP remains a scope limitation (arXiv:2403.03942#R2). These findings establish recurrence across settings rather than matched replication of one operational definition. Counts: versions.V4.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original is 0; versions.V4.studies_with_challenges is 1, corresponding to persistent failure of multi-fact chaining (arXiv:2607.08393#D03). Scale coverage is recorded in versions.V4.studies_by_size. The supplied versions.V4.studies_supports_only value of 0 predates the checker's reclassification of OLMoE domain curves as support.
suggested_status.open_questions: Independent reproduction of the OLMoE result with pre-specified pairing and evaluation would strengthen the billion-parameter pretraining evidence. Dense billion-parameter and larger-model pretraining trajectories would extend scale coverage. Matched delay measurements, including gradual improvement and failed generalization cases, would clarify which operational forms reproduce; a sharp or synchronous transition is not required by V4.

source.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
source.authors: Alethea Power; Yuri Burda; Harrison Edwards; Igor Babuschkin; Vedant Misra

original_result.result: The original paper did not test this claim.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Llama copying accuracy surged during pretraining after loss and in-context learning performance stabilized.
BERT improved on HANS long after in-distribution accuracy saturated during MNLI fine-tuning.
The OLMoE model’s math benchmark scores rose sharply after the corresponding training objectives stopped improving.
Models generalized grammar to new examples after learning training examples early in pretraining on C4 data.
Intersection generalization saturated well after memorization across four fully fine-tuned models.
A Wikitext-103 pretraining run showed no sudden transition from memorization to generalization.
Lower learning rates delayed and weakened copying emergence during pretraining.
BERT showed weaker delayed gains on PAWS-QQP and failed to generalize on some HANS subcases.
OLMoE showed separate delayed gains at different times, with no single, simultaneous overall transition.
Single-example reinforcement learning produced gradual gains after saturation; full-dataset training showed no such phase.
The measured delay in generalizing selected grammar patterns varied by pattern and by accuracy threshold.
Chaining often failed to generalize, while LoRA intersection fine-tuning showed minimal delays.
Models failed to generalize by linking facts step by step despite high memorization and extended fine-tuning.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Delayed generalization in models in the 10–100B and >100B size buckets.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size and versions.V4.coverage_by_operation contain no 10–100B or >100B bucket. The pack's pretraining and fine-tuning coverage does not supply results at those scales.

untested.what: Delayed generalization during realistic-text pretraining of dense, billion-parameter language models.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V4.coverage_by_operation supplies family, size and stage margins rather than their joint distribution. The pack's billion-parameter pretraining evidence is OLMoE; its dense pretraining evidence is sub-billion. The OLMoE header explicitly lists dense LLMs as untested.

wording_issues.issue: The studies use different reference events: ID validation saturation, pretraining-loss stabilization, critical-phrase exposure thresholds and paired training-objective plateaus. These operationalizations do not establish the same memorization-to-generalization transition.

Realistic training corpora coexist with restricted evaluation protocols: synthetic context copying, selected grammatical exposure splits and per-fact knowledge-graph injection. These results do not establish delayed improvement across general natural-language capabilities.
OLMoE's benchmark evidence is evaluated through additional LoRA instruction tuning at pretraining checkpoints. The measured trajectory therefore depends on that evaluation procedure.

method_sensitivity.factor: Optimization clock, batch size and learning rate
method_sensitivity.what: For 162M Llama copying, onset aligns with approximately 38,000 update steps across batch-size variations rather than a fixed token count. Lower learning rates give later and weaker development. The row corrections flag an inconsistency in the source's learning-rate reporting.

BERT's delayed gain differs between MNLI/HANS and QQP/PAWS-QQP. HANS delayed improvement includes additional subcases shown in Appendix C, Figure 10; the reported failure to generalize concerns subcases not shown there. The selected OOD evaluation changes whether a delay followed by improvement is observed.

OLMoE 7B domain aggregates show local, asynchronous delayed generalization with stable gains across math, code, commonsense QA and domain-specific QA; no globally synchronous transition is reported. Retrospectively selected math training–test groups, formed using memorization/correctness trajectories and embedding-based Hungarian pairing, show benchmark leaps with annotated delays of 120k, 365k, 370k and 485k pretraining steps. Benchmark evaluation uses LoRA instruction tuning. These measurements depend on the aggregation and selected groups; both the domain curves and paired-group results support delayed generalization under V4, which requires neither global synchrony nor a sharp jump.

method_sensitivity.factor: Grammatical phenomenon, seed and validation threshold
method_sensitivity.what: In 60M models during early C4 pretraining, exposure-based lag varies across grammatical phenomena and seeds. Table 6 includes significant positive lags, a non-significant positive lag and zero lags. DNA1 Run 3 has a 100-step lag, p=0.087 against matched random splits, classified as absent; DNA2 has zero lag in every seed. Table 5 shows threshold-sensitive proxy-validation transition checkpoints, without corresponding proxy-train crossing times, so it does not establish threshold-sensitive train–validation lags.

One-example RLVR produces gradual gains after training saturation, whereas full-set RLVR does not reach training saturation and test performance plateaus. The pack additionally reports sensitivity to entropy loss and rollout temperature outside the extracted rows.

method_sensitivity.factor: Fine-tuning scheme, reasoning task and fact protocol
method_sensitivity.what: STaRK-Prime per-fact intersection has a substantial delay under full fine-tuning and a minimal delay under LoRA. Qwen-2.5-1.5B LoRA intersection has a positive average lag of 0.5 epoch, classified as partial; absence or statistical negligibility is not established. Per-fact chaining often fails to generalize, while multi-fact chaining remains poor despite memorization. Reported generalization times exclude failed cases.
